title: Asking for a raise
tagline: Learn to ask for a raise confidently, handle budget objections, and negotiate your total compensation package.
you_are: an employee who has had a strong year and wants a salary increase
setting: Private one-on-one meetings with your direct manager in an office or on a video call to discuss performance and compensation.

scenarios.label: Request the meeting
scenarios.desc: Ask your manager for a dedicated time to discuss your role and compensation.
scenarios.setup: You catch your manager at their desk or send a calendar invite. They glance up and say, “Sure, what’s this about?”
scenarios.objective: Secure a private, formal meeting to discuss your compensation within the next week.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 10:15 am, quiet morning before meetings start

scenarios.label: Present your case
scenarios.desc: Walk through your achievements and ask for a specific increase.
scenarios.setup: You sit down in the booked room. Your manager opens with, “Thanks for pulling the numbers together. Walk me through what you’ve got.”
scenarios.objective: Present quantified achievements and request a concrete salary figure or percentage increase.
scenarios.moment: Thursday 2:00 pm, afternoon light through blinds

scenarios.label: Handle objections
scenarios.desc: Respond to budget limits, timing issues, or a partial offer and negotiate the full package.
scenarios.setup: After your ask, your manager leans back and says, “I’d love to do that number, but the budget cycle is locked until Q3. What else could work?”
scenarios.objective: Negotiate alternative compensation elements and agree on a clear timeline or criteria for the raise.
scenarios.moment: Thursday 2:20 pm, tension easing into problem-solving

objections: We don’t have any budget left this year
The timing isn’t right with the fiscal quarter ending
Your performance metrics aren’t quite at the target level
We need to see more long‑term results before adjusting pay
A raise would set a precedent for others in the team
We prefer to keep compensation discussions separate from performance reviews
Our compensation committee meets only quarterly
We can only consider non‑salary benefits as alternatives

rubric.label: Professional framing
rubric.what: Opens the conversation respectfully, sets a collaborative tone, and avoids ultimatums or emotional language.

rubric.label: Evidence-based case
rubric.what: Cites specific achievements, metrics, and market data to justify the request without exaggeration.

rubric.label: Specific ask
rubric.what: States a clear dollar amount or percentage increase rather than a vague desire for more money.

rubric.label: Package negotiation
rubric.what: Explores bonus, equity, benefits, flexibility, or development budget when base salary cannot move.

rubric.label: Objection handling
rubric.what: Acknowledges budget or timing constraints calmly and pivots to actionable alternatives or future milestones.

rubric.label: Compliance integrity
rubric.what: Keeps discussion within company policy, avoids sharing protected salary data, and documents agreements accurately.

pitfalls: Threatening to quit or mentioning other offers as leverage before exploring internal options.
Asking for a range instead of a specific figure, which weakens anchoring.
Accepting a verbal promise without a follow-up email confirming the agreed timeline or criteria.
line: Asking my manager for a raise after a strong year

research.text: When asking your manager for a raise, anticipate objections such as budget constraints or timing concerns, and prepare responses that acknowledge these while keeping the conversation moving. Be ready to negotiate the entire compensation package, not just the base salary, and use specific dollar figures rather than vague requests. Request a private, formal meeting to discuss your role and compensation, and take notes during the conversation to follow up with an email summarizing the discussion. If your request is denied, ask for specific feedback on what would need to change for a future discussion. Sources emphasize the importance of professionalism and respect throughout the process, regardless of the outcome.
